ai.title: Track followup click events in CLI chat
ai.summary: Added AnalyticsEvent.FOLLOWUP_CLICKED and instrumentation in cli/src/chat.tsx to track user interactions with followup suggestions. The handler now logs prompt length, index, and agent mode via logger and sends the event to analytics before submitting the prompt. Includes promise handling for onSubmitPrompt to log success or failure. Scope covers CLI chat component and shared analytics constants.

eli5.text: When you click one of the quick-reply suggestions that appear under the assistant's answers in the chat, that click is now counted as an interaction. The click sends a short log entry (including how long the suggested reply was, which suggestion it was, and which mode the assistant was in) to the telemetry stream before the reply gets sent. You don't see anything new on screen, but each follow-up suggestion you tap is now recorded for analytics.

ai.title: Add debug logging to CLI message queue and send hooks
ai.summary: Instrumented `use-message-queue.ts` and `use-send-message.ts` with granular logging to diagnose input processing stalls. Queue processing logic now logs specific block reasons (e.g., `streamStatus`, `activeAgentStreams`) instead of silent returns. `use-send-message.ts` adds defensive state resets in `finally` blocks and logs validation failures and SDK run configs.

eli5.text: When you send a message in the CLI and nothing appears to happen, the application will now record exactly why it stopped, whether the conversation is still streaming, a previous action is still running, or new messages are waiting. Any developer who opens the logs to investigate a stalled message will see that blocked queue spelled out instead of a silent stop, and the send routine now clears leftover state even if something goes wrong. This makes it immediately live in the CLI for anyone troubleshooting a message that did not go through.

ai.title: Add e2e database setup and Playwright infrastructure
ai.summary: Introduced dedicated Postgres container (port 5433) and migration scripts via packages/internal/src/db/e2e-setup.ts for web E2E tests. Nightly CI now runs full `bun run e2e` suite instead of docs-only tests, with automatic cleanup. `web/package.json` scripts chain `e2e:setup` before Playwright execution; `playwright.config.ts` injects `E2E_DATABASE_URL` into webServer env. Remote DB safeguard requires `ALLOW_REMOTE_E2E_DATABASE=true` to bypass localhost check.

eli5.text: The nightly check that makes sure the app works end-to-end now tests the full website instead of just the documentation pages. It does this by spinning up a throwaway database, loading the right test data into it, running the complete set of simulated user journeys against the live web app, and then tearing the database down when it's done, so each run starts from a clean slate. A safety switch makes sure this only ever happens against a local database unless explicitly told otherwise, so test migrations never accidentally run against a production system. If you watched the nightly report, you'd see far more detailed browser-based test results covering real website flows rather than just doc-page checks.

ai.title: SDK loads knowledge files from user home directory
ai.summary: SDK auto-discovers user knowledge files (~/.knowledge.md, ~/.AGENTS.md, ~/.CLAUDE.md) from the home directory, merging them with project context. New `userKnowledgeFiles` option in `run()` allows overriding or extending these defaults. Priority logic (knowledge.md > AGENTS.md > CLAUDE.md) is centralized in `common/src/constants/knowledge.ts` and applied across CLI init, Agent Runtime prompts, and Evals. Home directory files are read-only for the agent.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant on a project, it now also reads a set of notes you keep for yourself in your home folder (files named knowledge.md, AGENTS.md, or CLAUDE.md), combining those with the project-specific notes so you get both your personal defaults and the project’s context. The tool looks in your home folder for those files and treats them as read-only, meaning it won’t edit your personal notes. If you don’t want that behavior, you can pass a new option when starting the assistant to point it at different files instead. You will notice the change the next time you use the assistant on a project, because your personal notes will start influencing how it responds without you having to copy them into each project.

eli5.text: When you attach files to a message in the CLI chat, it now treats both images and text files as the same kind of thing instead of handling them separately. The shared attachment preview card that shows next to your message now supports both media types through one consistent interface, and removing an attachment works the same way whether it's a picture or a document. This is live today and affects anyone using the CLI to chat with attachments.

ai.title: Add --paste and --retry to tmux-send.sh
ai.summary: Added --paste flag using bracketed paste mode and --retry for session detection in scripts/tmux/tmux-send.sh. --paste triggers CLI paste handler correctly vs raw keystroke; --no-enter skips submit. Retry defaults to 3 attempts with 0.3s delay. Updated scripts/tmux/README.md with usage examples.

eli5.text: If you use the helper script that sends text into a running tmux session, you can now paste the current clipboard contents instead of typing or sending one keystroke at a time. Pasting now happens through the terminal's proper paste mechanism, so the text arrives as a single block rather than as raw keystrokes that can get scrambled, and you can choose whether or not to press Enter afterward with a new option. The script will also try a few times to find your session before giving up if it's not ready yet, and the example commands in the documentation now show how to use these paste and automatic-retry features.

ai.title: Add Claude 4 Sonnet aliases to OpenRouter mapping
ai.summary: Added `anthropic/claude-4-sonnet-20250522` and `anthropic/claude-4-sonnet` keys to `OPENROUTER_TO_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_MAP` in `common/src/constants/claude-oauth.ts`. Both aliases resolve to the canonical `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` model ID. This ensures correct routing for OpenRouter requests using these specific model identifiers.

eli5.text: If you ask the assistant through OpenRouter using a model name like "claude-4-sonnet" or "claude-4-sonnet-20250522," the system now correctly recognizes it as the same model as "claude-sonnet-4-20250514." Previously, those slightly different names might have caused confusion or failed to connect to the right version; now they all point to the same one.

ai.title: Ad impression credit floor randomized
ai.summary: Ad impression credit grants now use a randomized minimum floor instead of a static constant. The `MINIMUM_CREDITS_GRANTED` value is increased by a random integer between 0 and 2 using `Math.floor(3 * Math.random())`. This change affects the ad impression payout logic in `web/src/app/api/v1/ads/impression/_post.ts`, ensuring variable minimum credit grants per impression.

eli5.text: When someone sees an ad, the system gives them a small number of free credits, but now the smallest amount they can get will vary a little instead of always being the same. The change only affects how that minimum credit amount is picked, so you still get at least something every time, just maybe one or two more credits than before on some views. It's live now, and the only difference you'd notice is that the tiny credit reward isn't always exactly the same low amount.

eli5.text: The testing system that checks terminal-based AI assistants now works with multiple assistants instead of just one. Previously, the system could only automate tests for a single AI coding tool called Codebuff. Now it can also automatically test two other popular AI coding assistants - Claude Code and Codex - using the same terminal automation approach. The developer who runs the tests writes a description of what to check (like 'verify the help screen looks right'), and the system spawns a simulated terminal session, sends the commands, captures what appears on screen, and reports back whether it worked. All session activity is logged to a debug folder so anyone can review exactly what happened during testing.

ai.title: CLI release 1.0.584 ships unified attachments, home-dir knowledge
ai.summary: Version 1.0.584 aggregates fourteen changes across the CLI, web, SDK, agent runtime, and scripts. The CLI adopts a unified PendingAttachment type replacing pendingImages, raises LONG_TEXT_THRESHOLD from 200 to 1000 chars so shorter pastes insert inline, and fixes credential saving to merge rather than overwrite entries. The SDK auto-discovers user knowledge files from the home directory with a knowledge.md > AGENTS.md > CLAUDE.md priority, while tmux-send.sh gains --paste and --retry flags and the generic TUI testing infrastructure adds Claude Code and Codex tester agents. Ad impression payout floors are now randomized, saveUserCredentials pretty-prints JSON, and AnalyticsEvent.FOLLOWUP_CLICKED tracks followup suggestion clicks; this release also restores OpenRouter routing for Claude 4 Sonnet aliases and adds e2e Postgres setup with E2E_DATABASE_URL injection.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json hunk changes codebuff version from 1.0.583 to 1.0.584; release updates list 14 changes dated 2026-01-15 through 2026-01-16 covering CLI auth, ad credits, analytics, debug logging, E2E infra, SDK knowledge files, unified attachments, tmux paste/retry, Claude 4 Sonnet aliases, randomized ad floor, generic tmux TUI testing, and LONG_TEXT_THRESHOLD increase.

eli5.text: This release brings smarter personal knowledge handling, unified attachment management, and new model support to the command-line tool. You can now have your personal notes and instructions files (like a custom knowledge file, AGENTS.md, or CLAUDE.md) automatically discovered from your home directory and merged with your project context, so the assistant starts with your preferred setup every time. Attaching both images and text files is now handled through one consistent system, making file sharing smoother and preparing the tool for broader attachment types in the future. The tool now recognizes new Claude 4 Sonnet model variants from OpenRouter, and ad credit payouts use a randomized minimum floor to keep earnings fairer per impression. Automated end-to-end testing infrastructure was added so future updates can be checked more thoroughly before reaching you.

ai.summary: scripts/tmux/tmux-send.sh clears input buffers via C-u and adds delays to prevent command concatenation. scripts/tmux/tmux-start.sh generates unique session names using PID and random suffix to avoid parallel collisions. Deduplication state is now explicitly reset during session initialization.

eli5.text: When multiple automated assistants work at the same time in separate terminal windows, they can now start up using their own unique session names instead of crashing into each other. Each session now gets a name that includes the computer's process number and a random number, so two assistants won't accidentally share or mix up their workspaces. Additionally, the commands you send to these terminal sessions are now spaced out with tiny pauses, and any leftover text in the input line gets wiped clean before new commands are typed, preventing your instructions from accidentally running together into nonsense.

ai.title: Fix Ctrl+J newline insertion in CLI multiline input
ai.summary: Ctrl+J now inserts a newline in CLI multiline input by detecting the terminal-translated linefeed character (0x0a) or ctrl+j key sequence. Previous logic missed linefeed detection, causing Ctrl+J to fail. Scope limited to cli/src/components/multiline-input.tsx. Key check prioritizes linefeed name over raw ctrl+j to handle terminal translation.

eli5.text: When you're typing a long message across multiple lines in the command-line version of the assistant, pressing Ctrl+J now reliably starts a new line instead of being ignored or acting like Enter. Previously, the software only recognized Ctrl+J when it arrived as the raw two-key combination, but most terminals quietly translate Ctrl+J into a linefeed character before the assistant ever sees it, so the shortcut silently failed. The fix tells the input field to also watch for that linefeed character and treat it the same as Ctrl+J, making the shortcut work consistently in regular terminal windows today.
